subject: Urgent: Model13k-v2.1 latency spike — request for temporary SLA carveout and rollback authorization
message_1_header:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Samir Rao <samir@nebulapay.com>, Procurement <procurement@nebulapay.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production p95 jump for NebulaPay - model13k-v2.1 rollout
message_1_body:
Folks,

We observed a sustained p95 latency increase for NebulaPay beginning ~08:45 PDT after the staged rollout of model13k-v2.1. Key datapoints:
- Baseline p95 (previous 7d): 180 ms
- Current p95 (impact window): 560 ms
- Error rates unchanged; tail appears to be compute-bound when sequence lengths >512 tokens.

The rollout touched 60% of NebulaPay traffic (canary -> ramp). Traffic patterns show a higher-than-expected token-length distribution for this customer, which triggers an expensive attention kernel in v2.1. Immediate mitigation options we can execute within the hour:
1) Activate variant fallback to model13k-v2.1-quant-lite (lower perf but avoids kernel path); estimated quality delta ~1.2% measured on recent evals.
2) Roll back to model13k-v2.0 (stable) — requires coordination and a short maintenance window (we estimate 30–45m).
3) Apply a temporary traffic cap (pin) for NebulaPay while we triage.

Ask: We need authorization from product/ops + commercial to approve a temporary SLA carveout for the duration of the mitigation and permission to proceed with a rollback if variant fallback fails. Samir / Procurement: please confirm whether NebulaPay can accept a short window where we operate under an exception and the proposed remediation steps.

I've attached the live dashboard snapshot and a CSV of sample requests for the last 45 minutes. Will follow with more detail from infra.

Ben
Senior Account Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: latency_dashboard_qps.png, latency_samples.csv
message_2_header:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production p95 jump for NebulaPay - model13k-v2.1 rollout
message_2_body:
Thanks, Ben — and Samir, sorry you're seeing this.

Quick questions before we lock a plan:
- Karthik: can you confirm whether the regression is isolated to model13k-v2.1 or also visible on canary hosts with different kernel selections?
- Kim: what's our expected customer-facing SLA impact if we pin NebulaPay to v2.0 for 1 hour? Will that trigger an automatic credit per contract?

Immediate ask from my side: please prepare a short mutual action plan (MAP) that includes rollback timing, expected customer impact, and a proposed carveout period for the SLA. If rollback is lowest risk, I want a play-by-play and a runbook we can share with NebulaPay procurement for signoff.

Samir — if you can confirm acceptance of a temporary exception (we'll document exact minutes and will notify your team before action), we will proceed. We prioritize minimizing user disruption.

Olga
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
message_3_header:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Samir Rao <samir@nebulapay.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production p95 jump for NebulaPay - model13k-v2.1 rollout
message_3_body:
Olga / team — quick technical summary and recommended path: 

Root cause (prelim): new attention kernel selection in v2.1 triggers an O(seq^2) memory access pattern for sequences >512 tokens on our current GPU kernel path. For NebulaPay's request profile this yields queuing that shows up as p95 spikes without increasing 5xxs.

Options and risk notes:
- Variant fallback (model13k-v2.1-quant-lite): fast to flip (config change). Pros: <5 min to deploy; minimal traffic disruption. Cons: small quality regression; unknown edge-case behaviours for structured outputs.
- Rollback to model13k-v2.0: safer for quality parity and known perf. Operational risk: ~30–45 min maintenance window to drain and re-pin hosts; requires coordination with infra and commercial (customer notice).

Suggested plan and timeline: 
1) If customer accepts exception: authorize a 2-hour SLA carveout window starting at 02:00 UTC on 2027-07-08.
2) At T+0 (02:00 UTC) we will attempt variant fallback. If p95 remains >350 ms after 10 min, initiate rollback at T+15 min.
3) Post-action: capture perf traces, validate p95 back to baseline, and run a brief quality smoke test against the MAP prompt set.

Attached: rollback_playbook_v2.md (runbook with step-by-step commands, rollback safety checks, and rollback verification script).

Karthik
Staff SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rollback_playbook_v2.md

Subject: Re: Production p95 jump for NebulaPay - model13k-v2.1 rollout
message_4_body:
Olga / team — thanks for the rapid response and the clear plan. We accept the proposed course: a 02:00 UTC window and the variant-fallback-first approach with rollback contingency. A few notes from us: 

- Procurement is fine with a documented temporary carveout for the exact duration of the remediation; we will expect an itemized note for credits if the final p95 averages above the contract SLA for a full 24-hour window around the event.
- Please send a confirmation email 30 minutes prior to the 02:00 UTC action with the exact steps and expected customer-visible effects.

We appreciate the transparency. Once the rollback is complete, please share the incident write-up and perf traces so we can close the loop internally.

Samir Rao
Head of Platform Engineering
NebulaPay
